rule.description: A function signature receives a group of three or more parameters that recurs, name for name and type for type after borrows, mutability, and lifetimes are erased, in at least one other signature of the same crate — data threaded through signatures unchanged instead of being held behind one abstraction.

checks.description: Detect function signatures that carry a group of at least three parameters which another signature in the same crate carries with the same names and equivalent types, so the group is really one piece of data handed around piecewise.
checks.detected_relation: function signature -> group of >=3 parameters recurring, by name and normalized type, in another signature of the same crate
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The group describes one set of data — the CLI output options, the tape-build context — that arrives unchanged at every stop; passing it as loose parameters at each signature is the poor encapsulation a missing abstraction produces.

matches.evidence: process_json(json, query, validate, inline, raw_string, sort_keys, evaluator) receives the three output options separately and shares the group `inline`, `raw_string`, `sort_keys` with format_json; the options had a single owner record before the step that threading them apart belongs to.

format_json(result, inline, raw_string, sort_keys) receives the same three output options separately, so every caller of the pair — main's three input paths and the two tests — repeats the names at both signatures.

tape_in_place(buffers, tokens, json) takes the tape-build context `buffers`, `tokens`, `json` as free parameters and shares the group with tape_escaped; the buffers and the input belong to the evaluator that previously held the whole build.

tape_escaped(buffers, tokens, json, copy) repeats the same three context parameters plus its scratch copy, one of two sibling signatures threaded with the identical group where the escaped-input branch used to reach for the evaluator's own state.

excluded.reason: Pairs such as `tokens`, `json` that always travel together are two parameters, not a group of three or more; the rule does not reach them.
The parser passes groups as tuple-typed single parameters rather than as loose recurring parameters, which is already an encapsulation the rule accepts.
